newsitem.title: ST VINCENT AND THE GRENADINES: Caribbean nation hires firm to boost image.
newsitem.headline: Caribbean nation hires firm to boost image.

text.p: The Caribbean nation of St. Vincent said on Wednesday it had hired a U.S. public relations firm to counteract negative publicity brought by the arrest of an American couple on murder charges.
"It will be an ongoing project," Prime Minister James Mitchell said of the group called West Indies Communication Group, which has already begun work on research.
He said the group initially would be paid $15,000, but the full campaign, which would include television in the United States, would cost more.

James and Penny Fletcher, a wealthy couple from West Virginia, have been in prison in St. Vincent since last fall. They are expected to go on trial later this summer for the Oct. 9 murder of Jerome "Jolly" Joseph, a water taxi driver who was found shot to death.
The case recently was reported on the ABC television programme "20/20," which criticised the St. Vincent government and said the couple could not get a fair trial because of corruption on the island.

The show linked the Fletchers' case with that of Allan Heath, a South African who was suspected of murdering his wife in St. Vincent last November and then alleged he had to bribe island police to win his freedom.
The Caribbean News Agency (CANA) reported that Mitchell invited the South African police to conduct an investigation into the incident, but had not received a response.
U.S. President Bill Clinton interceded on the couple's behalf with Mitchell during a visit to Barbados last month, asking that they receive due process, the CANA reported on Wednesday.
CANA also reported that at least one hotelier in St. Vincent had reported cancellations from some repeat U.S. visitors as a result of publicity surrounding the case.
